requirements.evidence: Contract matches task: enum CallMode with the three string cases (app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:31-35). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB (lines 38-46); ordering priority desc / issued_at / id (line 116), normal_only oldest-first (line 109), priority_only filter (line 113); fairness uses last 3 calls by called_at desc, id desc in this queue across all modes and requires a waiting normal (lines 123-145); candidate row locked and re-checked, skipped ids excluded on retry (lines 76-85); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id written and the saved model returned (lines 87-92). Docs updated in business-rules.md and architecture.md 'Call the next ticket'.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php as one invokable class; no service/repository layer; reuses InactiveQueueException; PHPDoc on the public __invoke and helpers; tests ship with the change (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php); docs kept in sync including CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry (CHANGELOG.md:21) and docs/database-schema.md write-once note.

security.evidence: Task explicitly excludes authorization ('the caller is trusted'); docs state authorization stays with the caller (docs/business-rules.md:104). No mass assignment (explicit attribute sets at CallNextTicket.php:87-90), stale Queue instance is not trusted (lines 38-41), concurrency handled by row locks; no user input or output surfaces.

tests.evidence: 19 Pest tests cover ordering and id tie-break, queue/status isolation, returned model state, each mode, inactive and stale-queue rejection with no changes, NoWaitingTickets for all three empty cases, fairness trigger/reset/cross-mode history/no-normal-waiting/under-3/called_at+id tie/other-queue isolation, and the concurrent-skip path via a Ticket::retrieved hook (CallNextTicketTest.php:347-378). Small caveat: the 'falls back to priority' test (line 312) does not actually reach the fallback branch, because fairness is recomputed after the normal is called.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: one action, two small private helpers, a constant for the streak. The Any-mode fallback re-query (CallNextTicket.php:62-66) is effectively unreachable: fairnessApplies() is re-evaluated each loop iteration and only returns true when a waiting normal exists, which the restricted query would then find.

readability.evidence: Clear names (fairnessApplies, candidateQuery, FAIRNESS_STREAK) and useful comments on the locking/race reasoning (lines 37, 74-75). Small issues: the while(true)/continue loop with a nested fallback is a bit dense, and the comment at lines 59-61 describes a scenario that cannot happen.

scope.evidence: Only the action, enum, exception, tests and the related docs (business-rules, architecture, database-schema write-once note, CHANGELOG). No HTTP/Livewire/authorization added, matching 'Out of scope'.

issues.explanation: The Any-mode fallback to full ordering is effectively dead code: fairnessApplies() is recomputed on every iteration and returns true only when a waiting normal exists, so the restricted query never comes back empty when it is true.

'falls back to priority when the only normal ticket is called concurrently' passes because the concurrent normal call resets the streak, not because of the fallback branch, so the test name is misleading and the branch is untested.
The comment describes a race outcome (restricted set holding only excluded ids) that cannot occur given how fairness is recomputed, which could mislead future maintainers.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action, the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, matching the contract. Queue/ticket locking, deterministic ordering, all three modes and the fairness rule follow the task, and the change ships a thorough Pest suite plus synced docs and CHANGELOG. The only issues are an effectively unreachable fallback branch and a test whose name claims it covers that branch, so I would approve with nits.
